post: These students brought not only their civic knowledge to the national stage, they also brought ideas for their communities. Congratulations to the 2026 National Civics Bees top finishers: champion Peter Daniell of Colorado, second-place winner Araoluwakiitan Afolabi of Florida, and third-place winner Carolyn Taylor of Michigan. Together with their fellow finalists, they put their knowledge, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills to the test. BRI was proud to serve again as the official content partner of the National Civics Bee. Our work with the Bee has included study guides, competition questions, and educator resources that connect civic learning with the skills of citizenship. For us, the purpose extends well beyond the competition: helping students understand our founding principles, think for themselves, and prepare to contribute to our nation. Thank you to the U. S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation and its initiative, the Civic Trust, for bringing these young voices together. Meet the winners and explore the championship highlights:  https://bit.ly/4inmUQe  #NationalCivicsBee  #CivicEducation Photo credit: U. S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation

Lawtnee Frazier isnt looking for a classroom full of matching opinions. When her eighth graders consider whether Andrew Jackson should stay on the $20 bill, they study his presidency and support their answers with evidence. Some argue for keeping him; others want a replacement. What matters is how they make their case. Congratulations, Lawtnee, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the Quail Hollow Middle School teacher helping students think for themselves:  https://bit.ly/4jln8IE  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Christopher Klugman used to receive students' letters in a legislators office. Now he helps students write them. At BASIS Scottsdale in Arizona, his students study the Constitution, develop arguments, and write to elected officials. They're learning how to make a case and take part in civic life. Congratulations, Christopher, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institute's National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet Christopher:  https://bit.ly/3VR2S7Y  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Here's the part of the Civic Star Challenge that surprises people: Winners are selected by drawing. That means there's no panel scoring your teaching. No rubric. No one deciding whether your lesson was impressive enough. You share a real classroom moment, and you're in the drawing for $5,000. The ones who don't win are the ones who don't enter. Share your story today:  https://bit.ly/45xK27C  #CivicStarChallenge  #TeacherLife

Alishia Gaston Stack asks her students to propose a 28th Amendment. Then comes the challenge: making the case for it. At Lowndes High School in Valdosta, Georgia, students research their proposals, weigh the pros and cons, and present to classmates acting as Congress. They have to think beyond what they want changed to explain why it belongs in the Constitution. Congratulations, Alishia, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping students turn opinions into reasoned arguments:  https://bit.ly/4zy9LcY  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Monica Brown puts an important decision in her fourth graders hands: how will they help their community? At Oakshire Elementary School in Memphis, students investigate local needs, choose a service project, and carry it out with help from family and community members. They get practice making thoughtful decisions and taking responsibility for what happens next. Congratulations, Monica, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping young students put civic responsibility into practice:  https://lnkd.in/e_4GMnp7  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Patricia Wyskowski wants her students to know when to trust a source and when to keep digging. At Bayonne High School in New Jersey, students investigate a sources origins and ask what else they need to know. She wants that habit of questioning and checking to stay with them as they become voters. Congratulations, Patricia, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Get to know Patricia:  https://bit.ly/3VEKP4S  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

In 2025, BRI ran 315 professional development programs across 27 states and Washington, D. C., reaching over 8,000 teachers. The programs we're most proud of aren't the ones with the highest single-day turnout. They're the ones where we're still showing up years later. Our PD is built around the Founding documents  the Declaration, the Constitution, the Bill of Rights  and the civic principles that come up in every election, every courtroom, and every classroom debate. We design programming to compound: each session builds on the last, and each year gives teachers a deeper foundation to teach from. What would your district's civics program look like with a PD partner for the next 3 years, not just the next 3 weeks? 🔗 Request a program:  https://bit.ly/4fZoZ46  #CivicsEducation  #ProfessionalDevelopment  #AmericanHistory  #K12Education  #ConstitutionDay

Seth Harris's seventh graders dont always get the verdict they hoped for. He makes sure they learn from it. After their mock trial, students examine which arguments persuaded the jury and why. Making their own case is only part of the work. They also have to understand how someone else reached a different conclusion. Congratulations to Seth Harris of Shaker Middle School in Latham, New York, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping students practice thoughtful disagreement:  https://bit.ly/4i74GCm  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Helping students evaluate information and disagree respectfully takes thoughtful teaching. That work deserves recognition. Congratulations to the latest Civic Star Challenge honorees! Together with iCivics, were recognizing teachers who connect the Declaration of Independence to the choices and responsibilities students encounter today. Thank you to Griffin Catalyst, The James Irvine Foundation, Stand Together Trust, and The Pederson Foundation for supporting the teachers behind this work. Meet the honorees:  https://bit.ly/4hG55u7  #CivicEducation  #TeacherAppreciation
